elaine: Quick flag  docs CI failed on the Optimize migration PR. snippet-exec + link-checker both tripped. :eyes:

elaine: Broken link reported to /optkit/quant-profiles (404) and the inline Python quant sample uses the old API (Precision + calibrate kw).

ryan: Can you paste the failing snippet?

elaine: Sure. Current example that fails CI:
```python
from redwood.optimize import QuantProfile
q = QuantProfile(precision='int8', calibrate=True)
```

sam: That matches what infra warned about. Since SDK 0.9 we use dtype + a calibrator object. Minimal replacement:
```python
from redwood.optimize import QuantProfile, DefaultCalibrator
q = QuantProfile(dtype='qint8', calibrator=DefaultCalibrator())
```

sam: Also, runtime YAML samples still use `kv_cache_enabled: true` in a few places. The runtime now accepts `kv_prefetch: auto|on|off`. Those don't break snippet-exec but confuse users.

elaine: Good call. I'll open a small PR to: 1) swap /optkit/quant-profiles -> /optimize/quantization, 2) update the Python snippet to the new API, and 3) grep/replace `kv_cache_enabled` -> `kv_prefetch: 'auto'` in docs examples. Kept minimal edits to ease review.

ryan: I'll add a quick smoke test under docs/tests/snippets/quant_profile_smoke.py that runs the example via snippet-exec and asserts the object has a `dtype` attribute. That should catch future API drift.

docs-bot: PR #999  snippet-exec: failed (1), link-checker: 2 broken links. Artifacts: https://ci.redwood.example/999/artifacts

elaine: Also adding a short migration note to the checklist: "SDK <0.9 -> >=0.9: replace QuantProfile(precision=...) with QuantProfile(dtype=...) and use a calibrator object (DefaultCalibrator) instead of calibrate=True."

sam: Ping me on the PR and I'll review the snippet changes. If CI is green after the fixes we can merge and proceed with the docs release.

ryan: Opening the tiny PR in ~15m and tagging @sam. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
